chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān narrated from Badr ibn Khalīl, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man who was in prison and said: “For Allah it is upon me that, if I leave this prison of mine, I will fast for a year.” Then the man came out of prison and feared that he might not be able to fast for a year. What should he do?

He عليه السلام said: “He should fast one month, and then from the second month some days, so that he will have fasted two consecutive months. Then after that he should continue fasting, and whenever he breaks for a day, he should give a mudd in charity; and whenever he fasts, it is counted for him, until a year is completed for him.”

key_terms.أَنْ أَصُومَ سَنَةً: to fast for a full year
key_terms.حُسِبَ لَهُ: it is counted for him toward fulfillment
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months without interruption at the outset
key_terms.لِلَّهِ عَلَيَّ: a formula of vow, meaning an obligation undertaken for Allah
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a mudd, a measure given as charity for a missed day

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they vowed to fast for a year but later fear they cannot complete it continuously?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a vow to fast for a year made upon release from imprisonment. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that the person begin with two consecutive months, then continue toward the full year, compensating missed days with a mudd of charity while counting the days he does fast.
